Reference / fs/file

fs/file#

A file is a resource: File opens it lazily, owns the handle and closes it once (close() is idempotent; destroy closes too).

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let file = File(path: Path("notes.txt"));
defer file.close();
let content = file.text().content();

Description#

A file is a resource: File opens it lazily, owns the handle and closes it once (close() is idempotent; destroy closes too). It is read and written through one of two symmetric views, and the first view used picks the mode; the other view then throws FileError.invalid_operation.

This compile-only example reads an existing UTF-8 notes.txt when used in a program. File I/O is not allowed in runnable documentation examples.

let file = File(path: Path("notes.txt"));            // reading, UTF-8 text
defer file.close();
for file.text() -> line { … }                  // line by line, in batches
let lines is @string = file.text().lines();    // the remaining lines
let all = file.text().content();               // the remaining text

let log = File(path: Path("app.log"), mode: FileMode.appending);
log.text().writeln("started");
log.close();

let image = File(path: Path("image.png"));
for image.binary() -> b { … }                  // byte by byte, in batches
let header is @byte = image.binary().bytes(8); // up to 8 bytes; [] at the end
let rest is @byte = image.binary().bytes();    // the remaining bytes
image.binary().seek(0, SeekOrigin.start);
text() binary()
for … -> lines bytes
next unit line() byte()
the rest as an array lines() bytes()
the whole as one value content() (bytes())
a piece — bytes(n)
where — offset(), seek(…), truncate(…)
write write(…), writeln(…), rewrite(…) write(source), <-
replace the whole file at once replace(…) replace(bytes)
make it durable sync() sync()

A whole file is one line each way, and the file closes when the File goes:

let notes = File(path: Path("notes.txt")).text().content();
let image is @byte = File(path: Path("image.png")).binary().bytes();
File(path: Path("notes.txt"), mode: FileMode.writing).text().write(notes);
File(path: Path("image.png"), mode: FileMode.writing).binary().write(image);

Writing so empties the file first, so a reader or a crash in the middle sees a part. replace writes a temporary file beside it and renames it over the old one, so the file at the path is the whole old content or the whole new one:

File(path: Path("config.json")).text().replace(json);
File(path: Path("image.png")).binary().replace(image);

replace is atomic and durable. Atomic: a reader, and a crash at any point, finds the old file or the new one, never a part; two replaces at once leave one of them whole. Durable: the new file is synchronized before the rename and its directory after it, so once replace returns the new content survives a crash or a power cut, as far as the system and the disk keep the promise of fsync (F_FULLFSYNC on macOS); a disk that lies about its cache can still lose it. Linux and macOS are supported; Windows is not.

replace works on the path, whatever the File's mode, and neither opens nor moves its handle: a File already open still reads the old file. The new file keeps the permission bits of the file it replaces (owner, group, others; through a link, the target's); a file that did not exist is made owner-only. It is a new file: hard links to the old one keep the old content, and its owner is whoever runs the program. A symbolic link at the path is itself replaced by the file, and its target is left alone. A directory at the path is refused. Any failure before the rename leaves the old file as it was and removes the temporary one. When the rename is done but the directory could not be synchronized, the new content is in place and the failure is FileError.failed("not_durable", …).

flush() hands written data to the operating system, which may still lose it in a crash; sync() makes it durable.

content(), lines(), bytes() and replace hold the whole file in memory. For a file of unknown size read a bounded piece, bytes(limit), or walk it with for.

A line loses its LF and one CR before it; a final unterminated line is a line. line() and byte() throw EndOfInput at the end. Text is strict UTF-8 unless File names another canonical encoding: utf-16-le, utf-16-be, utf-32-le, utf-32-be, ascii, latin-1; no byte order is inferred and BOMs are kept as text. for walks a view batch by batch (Batching, #465): the runtime reads about 64 KiB and cuts it into lines or hands it out as bytes.

lock(mode) takes a whole-file advisory lock without waiting: a lock in the way gives Maybe.none. locked(mode) tells whether the file is locked in mode now, by this process or another one (fs/lock).

let file = File(path: Path("counter.txt"), mode: FileMode.reading_and_writing);
defer file.close();
let lock = file.lock(FileLockMode.exclusive) else throw Busy.now;
let count = Number(file.text().content()).int();
file.text().rewrite((count + 1).string());

match guard.lock(FileLockMode.exclusive) {
    case Maybe.some(lock) { serve(); }
    case Maybe.none { Stdout().writeln("already running"); }
}

Public API#

enum FileMode#

enum FileMode = (reading, writing, appending, reading_and_writing, reading_and_appending)

How File opens its file: reading (the default), writing (emptied first), appending, or reading and writing or appending together.

  • reading: Opens an existing file for reading; writes are refused.
  • writing: Opens for writing, creating the file or truncating its contents.
  • appending: Opens for writing at the end, creating the file if absent.
  • reading_and_writing: Opens an existing file for reads and writes without truncation.
  • reading_and_appending: Reads and appends to the file, creating it if absent.

FileMode.reading#

reading

Opens an existing file for reading; writes are refused.

FileMode.writing#

writing

Opens for writing, creating the file or truncating its contents.

FileMode.appending#

appending

Opens for writing at the end, creating the file if absent.

FileMode.reading_and_writing#

reading_and_writing

Opens an existing file for reads and writes without truncation.

FileMode.reading_and_appending#

reading_and_appending

Reads and appends to the file, creating it if absent.

enum SeekOrigin#

enum SeekOrigin = (start, current, end)

Where a seek counts from.

  • start: Counts the byte offset from the beginning of the file.
  • current: Counts the byte offset from the current position.
  • end: Counts the byte offset from the end of the file.

SeekOrigin.start#

start

Counts the byte offset from the beginning of the file.

SeekOrigin.current#

current

Counts the byte offset from the current position.

SeekOrigin.end#

end

Counts the byte offset from the end of the file.
